validity.recommendation: Cross-check against P8036 (Mit Nama-Abu Sultan P.S. Gas Pipeline, 114 km / 16in) before treating P8079 as a standalone project. Confirm with GASCO/EGAS documentation whether 10th of Ramadan City has its own physically distinct lateral, or whether this PID should be folded into / cross-referenced with P8036 as a way-point along that trunk rather than tracked as a separate line.
validity.researcher_notes: Applied BOTH tests required for this cohort: (1) full-text search of the EGAS Annual Report 2018 (no mention of a discrete '10th of Ramadan' pipeline in the text -- pdftotext searched, nothing found) and (2) the MAP test (printed p.35 = PDF page 19, GASCO national gas grid map, rendered at native ~280ppi from the embedded raster to avoid the upsampling trap noted for other rows in this cohort). The map DOES show a '10th of Ramadan' node -- but it is the brown 'INDUSTRIAL AREA' icon type per the legend, not a distinct pipeline endpoint, and it sits directly ON the green 'Existing P/L' trunk labeled '16" 114 km' running from the Mit Nama/Cairo hub through Abu Za'bal to Abu Sultan/El Shabab. That length+diameter combination (114 km, 16in) is an EXACT match for GEM's own P8036 'Mit Nama-Abu Sultan P.S. Gas Pipeline' (Mit Nama->Ismalia, len=114.0, dia=16), which is already a separate tracked row in this same batch. No independent spur or second length label branches off toward the 10th of Ramadan icon on the map -- the only line reaching it is the same 16in trunk. Immediately beside the icon the map prints 'Natgas' as a second label, which (like 'Egypt Gas / Town Gas' labels elsewhere on the same map) reads as the local distribution company serving that node, not a pipeline name -- consistent with an independent corroborating source: an egyptoil-gas.com 2014 feature ('All lies in the infrastructure') which names 'National Gas Company' as the LDC covering 'El Sharkeya Governorate and 10th of Ramadan City' (verified live, contains both 'Ramadan' and 'National Gas' -- see proposed_refs). That source confirms 10th of Ramadan City receives natural gas distribution service generally; it does NOT name or describe any standalone transmission pipeline called '10th of Ramadan Gas Pipeline'. Net read: gas service to the city is real, but the specific claim that this is its own distinct 4.5 km / 16in transmission pipeline, separate from the P8036 trunk that visibly passes through the same point with an identical diameter, is unconfirmed and looks more likely to be a mis-derived read of the same map feature already captured as P8036. This is NOT a full retraction -- a short local tie-in lateral into an industrial-city gas station is a plausible, ordinary piece of infrastructure (and matches the pattern of other short laterals in this same 40-row cohort, e.g. P8072 Kima Aswan Industrial at 4 km) -- but no source distinguishes it from P8036's route, so the duplicate question should be resolved by a human before either row is edited.

validity.researcher_notes: The current cited ref (https://petro-mag.org/ar/Magazine/v?id=9da3b6c6-1d02-4f9d-b9eb-4de28a32bb9d) returns HTTP 200 but is a client-side-rendered single-page app (raw HTML is 24KB, contains an Angular-style 'ohsnap' notification div and 18 <script> tags, no article body). Both url_verifier and a rendered WebFetch pass independently confirmed the only visible content is the magazine's generic homepage/portal shell (nav, recent-news teasers, subscription info) -- zero occurrences of 'Ramadan'/'رمضان', 'operating', '4.5'/'4.50', or '16' as pipeline-relevant content. This is a genuine inability to verify (our tools cannot execute the site's JS to reach whatever article the deep link may point to), not a confirmed dead link -- so it is reported here as UNRESOLVED/unsupported rather than as a confirmed-bad citation. Separately: the 16in diameter this row carries is suspicious on its own terms, because it is identical to the diameter of the P8036 trunk segment that the EGAS grid map shows passing directly through the same '10th of Ramadan' point (see the duplicate finding above) -- a short lateral tapping a larger trunk would ordinarily step down in diameter, not match it exactly. No independent source (map, LDC feature, or the cited petro-mag.org page) states a 4.5 km figure for any 10th-of-Ramadan-specific segment.

summary: P8079 concern/duplicate (10th of Ramadan sits directly on P8036's 16in/114km Mit Nama-Abu Sultan trunk on the EGAS grid map, no separate spur shown -- cross-check before treating as standalone) + concern/spec (Length 4.5km & Diameter 16in unconfirmed by any source; current petro-mag.org ref is an unrenderable JS shell, no values verifiable). No fills staged. UNRESOLVED: Length, Diameter, Status all lack independent corroboration.
